data.title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Pushed for F-15 Airmen to Join '60 Minutes' Interview After Iran Shootdown
data.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and political appointees pushed for the two F-15 airmen whose plane was shot down over Iran in April to take part in a '60 Minutes' interview, according to multiple sources. CNN Breaking News posted on X, citing several sources familiar with the matter, said the effort involved senior political appointees.

The report said the push centered on the airmen involved in the April incident over Iran, though no further details were provided about whether the interview took place or what the airmen were asked to discuss.

data.title: Nidec To Withdraw From Cambodia Production Amid Thailand Border Dispute
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese motor maker Nidec will withdraw from production in Cambodia because of the impact of the border dispute with Thailand. The company is pulling back from the country as the dispute affects its operations.

data.title: Ripple Executive Says Corporate Treasuries Are Key Growth Opportunity for RLUSD
data.description:
Ripple Stablecoin Senior Vice President Jack McDonald said corporate treasuries are an important growth opportunity for RLUSD. According to Odaily, Ripple Treasury serves about 1,200 corporate treasury and CFO clients after Ripple acquired treasury management software provider GTreasury for $1 billion last year, and those clients handle about $13 trillion in transactions annually.

McDonald said RLUSD circulating supply has grown more than 50% over the past month, with about $1 billion on XRP Ledger and $1.4 billion on Ethereum. He added that RLUSD daily active volume has more than doubled since the start of the year, rising from about $200 million last month to about $750 million. Payments and capital markets are currently the two main use cases, and Ripple has worked with Franklin Templeton and DBS on tokenized money market funds and lending.

data.title: Uganda's Tooro Kingdom Buries Former Child King Amid Succession Row
data.description:
According to the BBC, Uganda's King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once the world's youngest reigning monarch, was buried on Saturday days after a dispute over who should succeed him. Oyo, 34, ruled the traditional kingdom of Tooro in western Uganda from the age of three and died last month while receiving cancer treatment in the United States.

Thousands of mourners lined the streets as his casket was taken to the royal tombs in Fort Portal for a private ceremony. TV presenter Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, 56, who was named by clan elders as the next monarch, reportedly cast nine coffee beans into Oyo's grave in a ritual marking the end of one reign and the start of another. But Oyo's family had earlier rejected Kijanangoma, his cousin, and Princess Ruth Komuntale said the late king left a 2022 will naming his young son as successor. The boy's identity has not been disclosed. Archbishop of the Church of Uganda Stephen Kazimba Mugalu and President Yoweri Museveni both called for unity, while the Babiito royal clan defended its choice of Kijanangoma.

data.title: Iran and Oman Reach Agreement on New Strait Route
data.description: According to Jin10, Tasnim News Agency, citing informed sources, reported that Iran and Oman reached an agreement in early Shahrivar in the Iranian calendar, around the end of August, after intensive technical and diplomatic consultations. The understanding between Iran and Oman will be formally announced soon, and foreign ministers from Gulf coastal states will attend the relevant meeting. According to the source close to the negotiating team, the understanding was reached only by Iran and Oman, while other countries will attend the meeting only to learn the details of the route and transit arrangements and to signal that they do not oppose the arrangement. The source said Iran and Oman agreed on a new route into and out of the Strait of Hormuz and its specific arrangements, with the inbound route into the Persian Gulf entirely within Iran's territorial waters and part of the outbound route also within Iran's territorial waters. Ships will pass through the route under Iran's arrangements. After the plan is implemented, the southern route that the United States has insisted on keeping open will be closed, which the source said was the main trigger for the recent renewed tensions. The source added that Iraq will also attend the meeting, but these countries are only being informed of the outcome of the Iran-Oman talks, and the decision on the specific details of the understanding was made during technical-level talks between Iran and Oman. The source stressed that the understanding does not mean the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened, and said Iran has conveyed seven conditions for reopening the strait to the U.S. through intermediaries; until those conditions are implemented and approved by Iran's highest-level institutions, the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed.

data.title: Electrum Releases Version 4.8.2 With Security Fixes for Bitcoin Wallets
data.description:
Bitcoin wallet Electrum has released version 4.8.2 with multiple security fixes and broader codebase hardening. According to Odaily, the update addresses a critical backup issue affecting some Lightning wallets that use non-deterministic keys and anchored channels, and it includes fixes based on reports from Bitcoin Red Team, Calle, l0rinc, haoxucu, and m0wer.

The release also strengthens Lightning HTLC validation, rejects malformed xpub and xprv keys that were previously accepted, expands security hardening across the codebase, and prevents the Android QR code scanner from reading screenshots. Electrum said affected users will see a warning when starting the wallet and should export a new backup, as older backups cannot correctly restore funds in this scenario. It is the third security-focused release from Electrum since July, following versions 4.8.0 and 4.8.1.

data.title: Bitcoin Suisse Says Bitcoin Could Add Distinct Portfolio Risk as Hyperscaler Spending Tops $800 Billion
data.description:

The firm also said Ethereum may benefit as artificial intelligence agents increasingly use programmable, onchain financial infrastructure.
